title.justification: The title 'Flexible Option Learning' is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper.

analysis.description: The paper discusses a method to improve option learning in reinforcement learning by enabling simultaneous updates of all relevant options rather than just the executing one. This method is integrated into hierarchical reinforcement learning frameworks to enhance performance and data efficiency across various domains.

type.justification: The paper includes empirical validation of the proposed method across a variety of tasks and experimental setups.
type.quote: We empirically verify the merits of our approach on a wide variety of domains, ranging from gridworlds using tabular representations...

name.justification: The paper's central theme revolves around improving the efficiency of option learning in reinforcement learning systems.
name.quote: Temporal abstraction in reinforcement learning (RL), offers the promise of improving generalization and knowledge transfer in complex environments...

name.justification: The paper focuses on integrating the proposed method into hierarchical reinforcement learning systems for improved performance.
name.quote: Our method can therefore be naturally adopted in most hierarchical RL frameworks.

name.justification: The paper references the option-critic architecture as a base for implementing the proposed extension to option learning.
name.quote: When we combine our approach with the option-critic algorithm for option discovery, we obtain significant improvements...

is_contributed.justification: The paper builds upon the existing option-critic architecture rather than introducing it as a new model.
is_contributed.quote: When we combine our approach with the option-critic algorithm for option discovery, we obtain significant improvements...

is_executed.justification: The paper details experiments conducted using this architecture to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
is_executed.quote: We empirically verify the merits of our approach...

is_compared.justification: The option-critic architecture is compared in terms of performance improvements with other methods within the experiments.
is_compared.quote: We compare our approach, multi-updates option critic (MOC), to the option-critic (OC) algorithm as well as a flat agent, denoted as actor-critic (AC).

referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper specifically cites this as the baseline architecture for implementing and testing their method.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Pierre-Luc Bacon, Jean Harb, and Doina Precup. The option-critic architecture. CoRR, abs/1609.05140, 2016. URL http://arxiv.org/abs/1609.05140.

name.justification: Proximal Policy Optimization is used as one of the policy optimization frameworks to verify the proposed method's compatibility and performance.
name.quote: We leverage the PPO algorithm [Schulman et al., 2017] to build our hierarchical agents.

is_contributed.justification: PPO is used as an existing framework rather than a new contribution by the authors.
is_contributed.quote: We leverage the PPO algorithm [Schulman et al., 2017] to build our hierarchical agents.

is_executed.justification: The paper mentions experimentation using PPO to test the proposed approach.
is_executed.quote: We leverage the PPO algorithm [Schulman et al., 2017] to build our hierarchical agents.

is_compared.justification: PPO is used as a baseline to compare the effectiveness of the proposed method.
is_compared.quote: In Figure 3: Transfer on MuJoco. In a-b-c) we compare the performance of our approach, MOC, to various hierarchical baselines and to a flat agent using PPO.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper references the original PPO paper for its implementation of hierarchical agents.
referenced_paper_title.quote: John Schulman, Filip Wolski, Prafulla Dhariwal, Alec Radford, and Oleg Klimov. Proximal policy optimization algorithms. CoRR, abs/1707.06347, 2017.

name.justification: The paper uses the synchronous variant of A3C (A2C) in its experiments.
name.quote: ...we validate this by building our hierarchichal implementations on top of the synchronous variant of the asynchronous advantage actor-critic algorithm [Mnih et al., 2016], that is the A2C algorithm...

is_contributed.justification: A3C is an established model used as a basis for experimentation.
is_contributed.quote: Asynchronous methods for deep reinforcement learning. CoRR, abs/1602.01783, 2016. URL http://arxiv.org/abs/1602.01783.

is_executed.justification: The paper describes using A2C for validating the hierarchical learning implementations.
is_executed.quote: ...we validate this by building our hierarchichal implementations on top of the synchronous variant of the asynchronous advantage actor-critic algorithm [Mnih et al., 2016], that is the A2C algorithm...

is_compared.justification: The A3C framework is part of the models compared during experimentation.
is_compared.quote: In our experiments we use the same value of η. For all experiments, the shaded area represents the 80% confidence interval.

referenced_paper_title.value: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning

referenced_paper_title.quote: Volodymyr Mnih, Adrià Puigdomènech Badia, Mehdi Mirza, Alex Graves, Timothy P. Lillicrap, Tim Harley, David Silver, and Koray Kavukcuoglu. Asynchronous methods for deep reinforcement learning. CoRR, abs/1602.01783, 2016. URL http://arxiv.org/abs/1602.01783.

name.justification: The paper uses the classic FourRooms domain as part of its experimental validation.
name.quote: Experimental Setup: We first evaluate our approach in the classic FourRooms domain [Sutton et al., 1999b] where the agent starts in a random location and has to navigate to the goal in the right hallway.

referenced_paper_title.value: Between MDPs and Semi-MDPs: A Framework for Temporal Abstraction in Reinforcement Learning
referenced_paper_title.justification: The FourRooms domain is established in the Sutton et al. (1999b) paper which significantly influences this study.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Richard S Sutton, Doina Precup, and Satinder Singh. Between MDPs and Semi-MDPs: A framework for temporal abstraction in reinforcement learning. Artificial intelligence, 112(1-2):181–211, 1999b.

name.justification: Experiments using continuous control tasks are conducted within the MuJoCo domain to test the deep RL setting.
name.quote: We first perform experiments in the MuJoco domain [Todorov et al., 2012] where both states and actions are continuous variables.

referenced_paper_title.value: MuJoCo: A Physics Engine for Model-Based Control
referenced_paper_title.justification: The original paper for MuJoCo by Todorov et al. is referenced when describing the experimental setup.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Emanuel Todorov, Tom Erez, and Yuval Tassa. Mujoco: A physics engine for model-based control. In IROS, pages 5026–5033. IEEE, 2012.

name.justification: MiniWorld is used for experiments involving first-person visual navigation to test high-dimensional tasks.
name.quote: Experimental Setup: In this section we verify how our approach extends to tasks with high dimensional inputs such as the first-person visual navigation domain of MiniWorld [Chevalier-Boisvert, 2018].

referenced_paper_title.justification: The MiniWorld paper by Chevalier-Boisvert is referenced to describe the visual navigation domain used.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Maxime Chevalier-Boisvert. gym-miniworld environment for openai gym. https://github.com/maximecb/gym-miniworld, 2018.
